title: First Week Safety and Productivity — Remote Onboard Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a compact, actionable checklist for the new hire’s first 7 calendar days when joining remotely. Focus areas: safety (physical and data), immediate productivity, and lowering cognitive load for both new hire and manager.

Scope and intended audience:
- People Ops (owners)
- Hiring managers and assigned buddies
- IT / Equipment provisioning
- New hire (self-serve copy)

Principles: 
- Remove friction: reduce the number of one-off tasks the new hire must track.
- Safety-first: physical ergonomics, secure access, and mental health signposts.
- Repeatable templates: manager and buddy check-ins are short, scheduled, and consistent.

Before Day 0 (offer accepted -> 48 hours before start)
- People Ops confirms equipment list and ship ETA to new hire. (IT ticket created: HR-XXXXX).
- Security: create temporary account credentials, enroll in SSO, seed MFA requirement email.
- Manager: block recurring 30-min daily check for days 1–5 labeled: "Day 1–5 quick sync — <name>".
- Buddy: assigned and introduced by email (include timezone, calendar link, 15-min intro slot on Day 1).
- New hire receives an "arrival packet" email with: agenda for Day 1, Slack channels to join, Confluence links, emergency contact, mental health resources, and a short list: "what to have ready" (photo ID for payroll, confirm shipping address).

Day 1 — Orientation (first 8 hours)
- Morning (90 min): Welcome + Team Kickoff
  - 9:00 CEO/People Ops recorded welcome (pre-recorded ok).
  - 9:20 Manager 1:1 (30 min) — role context, top 3 priorities for first 30/60/90 days, immediate expectations.
  - 10:00 Buddy: environment tour (Slack etiquette, where to find runbooks, how to raise incidents).
- Midday (IT & Security setup — 60–120 min)
  - Confirm SSO access, MFA enrolled, VPN installed, laptop encrypted, password manager provisioned (company account).
  - Confirm access to required repos, internal docs, and project trackers. Use checklist link: Confluence/Access-Checklist.
- Afternoon (30–60 min): Low-risk task to ship
  - New hire is given a small, well-scoped task that touches the actual stack (e.g., update a README, fix a typo in docs, run a local test). Purpose: confirm tooling works end-to-end and provide early sense of contribution.
- End of day (15 min): asynchronous reflection  - New hire fills short pulse: "Day 1: success blockers" (three fields: what worked, what blocked me, one question).

Days 2–3 — Tools & Team Integration
- Technical checklist: 
  - Developer: confirm local dev environment can build & run a test commit.
  - Non-dev: confirm access to primary SaaS tools (zendesk, amplitude, stripe, etc.) and templates.
- Safety checks (physical & mental):
  - Ergonomics tip sheet sent; people ops runs optional voucher flow for standing desk / monitor if needed.  - Manager schedules 1:1 to explicitly invite: "how are you feeling about workload and context?"
- Buddy tasks: pair for 2 hours shadowing workflows (ticket triage, code review flow, customer handoff).

Days 4–5 — Early Work Rhythm
- New hire: shipping a small deliverable scoped with manager (by EOD Day 5).
- Manager: run short retro with new hire on onboarding friction; capture 3 action items and assign owners.
- Security: run basic access audit (people ops + manager) to ensure no over/under perms.

Day 6–7 — Stabilize and Forward Plan
- New hire and manager co-create 30/60/90 draft goals (documented in Confluence).
- People Ops schedules a 1-week onboarding pulse survey (2–3 questions) to feed program metrics.
- Buddy hands off a 1-page "known unknowns" doc capturing ongoing orientation tasks.

Manager & Buddy Responsibilities (short checklist)
- Pre-start: calendar blocks, equipment confirmation, and intro email.
- Day 1: 30-min 1:1, buddy intro, confirm small ship task.
- Days 2–5: daily 15–30 min quick syncs; explicit psychological safety check at least twice.
- End of week: create 3-point improvement list and set next 30-day goals.

IT & Security Quick Items
- Mandatory: SSO + MFA, disk encryption, provisioning of company password manager, VPN setup, endpoint manager enrollment.
- Recommended: local backup plan, home-office network security tips, VPN split-tunnel instructions when needed.
- Elevated hires (privileged access): require additional 2FA token provisioning and a short access review on Day 3.

Physical Safety & Ergonomics
- Provide an ergonomics checklist (screen height, chair posture, lighting, breaks).
- Offer stipend / vendor list for ergonomic equipment; fast-path approval for medical needs.

Sample Low-friction "First Ship" Tasks (choose one depending on role)
- Engineering: fix flaky test or update README with local run commands.
- Product: draft a short product brief or write acceptance criteria for a tiny ticket.
- Support: respond to a non-critical inbound ticket with supervision.
- Sales/CS: mock call debrief and update customer notes template.

Measurement & Signals to Monitor (People Ops + Manager)
- Access success rate (percent of hires with all core accounts working by EOD Day 1). Target: 85%+.
- First-ship completion rate by Day 5. Target: 90% participation where applicable.
- New hire NPS / pulse at Day 7. Track actionable comments for process improvements.

Common blockers & remedies (fast fixes)
- Blocker: laptop delayed -> Remedy: temporary hosted dev environment (codespaces) + call with manager for async tasks.
- Blocker: MFA onboarding fails -> Remedy: escalate to security on-call and provide emergency OTP fallback.
- Blocker: timezone mismatch for buddy -> Remedy: asynchronous pairing doc + recorded walkthroughs; schedule overlap window.

Open questions for program iteration
- Should we require the "first ship" for all roles or only those where it’s meaningful? Pros/cons log to be maintained.
- Is the ergonomics stipend sufficient globally? Collect vendor list gaps by region.

Appendix: Useful links and templates
- Access checklist template: Confluence/Access-Checklist
- Day 1 pulse form (short): Confluence/Day1-Pulse-Form
- 30/60/90 goal template: Confluence/30-60-90-Template

Notes to reviewer:
- This playbook is intentionally short — designed to be embedded in the candidate arrival email as a single-page action plan.
- Feedback items: please flag anything that will add >15 min of friction to Day 1.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12: initial draft by Aisha Moreno
- 2025-02-18: incorporate IT feedback (Liam Chen)
- 2025-03-01: ergonomic stipend language clarified (Sophie Alvarez)
